question: Should AXorcist be distributed through `openclaw/homebrew-tap`, and should its formula install prebuilt release artifacts or build the Swift package from source?
rationale: The executable already exists, but artifact ownership, architecture support, signing expectations, and tap update policy are release-product choices that cannot be inferred safely from the package code.

options.title: Ship release binaries
options.body: Publish checksummed architecture-specific or universal artifacts and have the official tap install them without requiring a local Swift toolchain.

options.title: Build from source
options.body: Add an official formula that compiles the tagged Swift package, accepting the Swift toolchain dependency and longer installation path.

options.title: Retain manual installation
options.body: Keep SwiftPM build-and-copy as the supported CLI installation method and close the packaging request by explicit policy.

recommendation.title: Ship release binaries
recommendation.body: Publish checksummed architecture-specific or universal artifacts and have the official tap install them without requiring a local Swift toolchain.
